input.text: At the foot of the Western Hills, inside Beijing Botanical Garden's grounds, lies Wofo Temple — the Temple of the Reclining Buddha. Its treasure is exactly what the name promises: a bronze Buddha, more than five meters long, lying on one side in the posture of the historical Buddha's final rest — the Nirvana pose — one arm pillowing his head, serenity itself in cast metal. Cast in the Yuan dynasty around thirteen twenty-one, it is among the largest bronze reclining Buddhas in China, and the hall that holds it keeps a dim, hushed atmosphere that fits the subject. The temple began in the Tang dynasty and its gardens — magnolias in spring, wintersweet blooming in the cold of January — make it a four-seasons detour. Combine with the botanical garden's conservatory next door: garden morning, bronze afternoon, and the quietest famous Buddha in Beijing.
